behavior: AC1 — a neutral skill-invocation verb exists in the map vocabulary and resolves to claude's native tool
AC2 — a harness with no native equivalent declares it explicitly; the loader rejects a verb that is both mapped and unsupported, and one declared unsupported outside the vocabulary
AC3 — every persona record declaring skills also declares the capability, and the deployed agent's tools: actually names Skill; both guards fail red when broken
verification: cd cli && go test ./internal/harness/ -run TestEveryPersonaDeclaringSkillsCanInvokeThem && grep -q 'every deployed persona can invoke the skills its own gate demands' ../tests/verify-setup.bats

behavior: AC4, Claude box only (it reads this machine's gate ledger and Claude Code's subagent transcripts, so it exits 1 on a box where no persona has been dispatched): a gate skill-consumed record carrying agent_type is matched by a subagent transcript of that session whose meta.json names the same agentType and which invoked that skill. A record written by hand has no such transcript, so it does not pass.
verification: L="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/dotfiles/gate"; jq -r 'select(.outcome == "skill-consumed" and (.agent_type // "") != "") | "\(.session) \(.agent_type) \(.skill)"' "$L"/*.decisions.jsonl 2>/dev/null | sort -u | while read -r s a k; do for m in "$HOME"/.claude/projects/*/"$s"/subagents/*.meta.json; do [ -f "$m" ] && jq -e --arg a "$a" '.agentType == $a' "$m" >/dev/null && grep -q "\"skill\":\"$k\"" "${m%.meta.json}.jsonl" && echo dispatched; done; done | grep -q dispatched

behavior: AC5 — every gate path writes a durable record, including allow and 'role did not resolve', independent of stderr and exit code
AC6 — a warn decision is readable from the record alone after the session ends, naming the skills
AC7 — agent_type is carried in the record, on the skill path too, separate from the role requested and the role resolved
AC8 — the change propagates by deploy from the vault SSOT plus the repo map alone, and a re-run reports changed=0
verification: S=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$S/home" && HOME="$S/home" bash scripts/compile-harness.sh --deploy >/dev/null 2>&1 && cp -a "$S/home" "$S/snap" && HOME="$S/home" bash scripts/compile-harness.sh --deploy >/dev/null 2>&1 && diff -rq "$S/snap" "$S/home"

behavior: AC9 — every new check has a red-direction test that fails when the thing it guards is broken
